author: tomaka
body:
This PR replaces the `sled` database with SQLite.
SQLite has several advantages:

- It is extremely mature. No risk of database corruption, breaking changes, or weird slowness.
- There exists external tools that allow looking inside of an SQLite database. You can realistically stop smoldot and look at the database content manually, whereas with sled you'd have to write code for that.
- Having a strong relational database schema reduces complexity overall.
- SQLite seems to use around 0.8-0.9 kiB per block, compared to around 3.5kiB/block with sled. This is surprising, considering that the volume of data is strictly the same in both cases (there isn't anything stored after this PR that wasn't already stored before) and that sled has compression enabled.
- Initialization is considerably faster with SQLite. https://github.com/paritytech/smoldot/issues/678 is fixed.

One drawback of SQLite is that it requires a C compiler. However, `sled`, when compression is enabled, requires one as well. It is not realistic to run `sled` with compression disabled, as the database just explodes in size.

Another drawback is that the API of the Rust `sqlite` library is a bit tedious to use.

In terms of speed, syncing smoldot is capped by the Wasm verification speed, not by the database writing speed. Both sled and SQLite are the same here.

[Linked HW bridge PR](https://github.com/uwrobotics/uwrt_mars_rover_hw_bridge/pull/25)

The new CAN library is called CANInterface and manages 2 CANBuses. Our old CAN infrastructure is still supported by using CANBus the same way as we previously did instead of using CANInterface. Currently, apps/test-can has a simple test app showing how to use the new CAN library. Also see apps/test-can/include/CANConfig.h for setting up CAN message maps, this is how we will define all the CAN signals that a specific board will receive/transmit. One-shot messages aren't put in the message map and are instead processed by the CANMsgHandler.

Update:
CAN hw filter setup is currently broken for CAN bus 2 due to this [Mbed bug](https://github.com/ARMmbed/mbed-os/issues/14596). Currently waiting for the [fix](https://github.com/ARMmbed/mbed-os/pull/14612) to get approved.

body:
[CAN rearchitecture notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15vdVIMkG_4F-1X9uTqsn_lBBEgxPH9hCTVnR2D9pFlY/edit)

[Linked firmware repo PR](https://github.com/uwrobotics/MarsRover2020-firmware/pull/337)

The idea is to use the YAML file to define CAN messages and signals, and generate the rest (DBC file, C headers and source for managing message data structures) with [cantools](https://cantools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) and python scripts, all based on the YAML description. All auto-generated files are put under `can/generated`. CANMsgMap is a std::unordered_map wrapper (very much like the LookupTable but it's not const), I was hoping this could be shared by FW and SW.

The current CAN dev workflow is:
1. Update the uwrt_mars_rover_can.yaml file
2. Run `python3 scripts/generate_can.py` in the HW bridge repo root
3. Make the necessary app changes in FW or SW, using the yaml file and generated files as reference

author: jsha
body:
Introduce a first use of the `<details>` and `<summary>` tags as
replacements for the JS-built toggles. I think this has the potential to
replace all the JS toggles and generally clean up the JS, CSS, and HTML.

Split rendering of attributes into two cases: in the case where they are
rendered as descendents of a `<pre>` tag, where they use indent spaces and
newlines for formatting, matching their surrounding markup. In the case
where they are rendered as descendants of a `<code>` tag, they are
rendered as `<div>`. This let me clean up some fragile CSS that was
adjusting the margin-left of attributes depending on context.

Remove toggles for attributes. With the ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES filter, it's
rare for an item to have more than one attribute, so hiding attributes
behind a toggle doesn't save any screen space in the common case.

Fix a couple of invocations of `matches!` that didn't compile on my
machine.

Restore a conditional for the JS `createToggle` call that was causing
"Expand description" to show up spuriously on already-expanded
descriptions.

Add JS for auto-hide settings and hide all / show all.

Remove a z-index property and some font color tweaks made unnecessary
by the `<details>` toggles.

Add CSS for the `<details>` toggles.

Examples at:

https://hoffman-andrews.com/rust/item-hide/std/iter/trait.Iterator.html
https://hoffman-andrews.com/rust/item-hide/std/convert/trait.Into.html
https://hoffman-andrews.com/rust/item-hide/std/io/trait.Read.html
https://hoffman-andrews.com/rust/item-hide/std/option/enum.Option.html

Addition to https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/83337

v7.1.0

7.1.0 (2021-02-12)

TypeScript fixes

Thanks for your patience as we iterate and improve our TypeScript setup. We now should support TypeScript properly across all environments - we do not use export = which caused issues when compiling TS to ESM. Missing types such as Permission and ScreenshotOptions are now present, and we fixed an incorrect type for jsonValue().

emulateMediaFeatures color-gamut support

You can now pass color-gamut options into Page.emulateMediaFeatures:

await page.emulateMediaFeatures([
  { name: 'color-gamut', value: 'p3' },
]);
await page.evaluate(() => matchMedia('(color-gamut: srgb)').matches);

author: aro5000
body:
### Proposed changes

Adding `docker.socket` to be added in the disable command for the "rootfull" docker. If you do not add `docker.socket` then any docker command will re-enable `docker.service`. For example on a test machine:
```
aro@test01:~$ sudo systemctl disable --now docker.service
Synchronizing state of docker.service with SysV service script with /lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install.
Executing: /lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install disable docker
Removed /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/docker.service.
Warning: Stopping docker.service, but it can still be activated by:
  docker.socket
aro@test01:~$ sudo docker ps        <================== Running this command re-enables docker.service and output on the next line
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE     COMMAND   CREATED   STATUS    PORTS     NAMES
aro@test01:~$ sudo systemctl disable --now docker.service docker.socket
Synchronizing state of docker.service with SysV service script with /lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install.
Executing: /lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install disable docker
Removed /etc/systemd/system/sockets.target.wants/docker.socket.
aro@test01:~$ sudo docker ps  <========= After disabling both, this command no longer works
Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running?
```

author: gpanders
body:
#### Description

<!-- Note: it is best to make pull requests from a branch rather than from master -->
Add [nim](https://nim-lang.org) port.

Nim's install script wants to install everything under a `nim` subdirectory under whatever directory you provide to `install.sh`. So for example if we use `./install.sh /opt/local` this would create an `/opt/local/nim` directory, which we obviously don't want. So I copied what Go does and installed this directory under `/opt/local/lib` so that it creates `/opt/local/lib/nim`. Binaries (`nim`, `nimble`, `nimgrep`, and `nimsuggest`) are symlinked from that directory (e.g. `/opt/local/bin/nim -> /opt/local/lib/nim/bin/nim`).

author: booraz149
body:
**Big viruses as 'event' spawn**
A new 'event' which would spawn up to 4 virus that grow their size on spawn (Up to 400 max health I think)
The event complements recent update on viruses which allows big virus to split into smaller ones
The viruses are capped at 40 total viruses, while 4 of the big ones can be in the world.


**Small invasion 'event' change**
Just a small addition - if the event timer rolls invasion event while it's already in progress, the timer will be reduced to 1 minute or lower so it can roll a different event
This change is made so no event time goes "wasted"
